correctness.rationale: The nondegenerate radical multiplication pairing implies every nonzero proper ideal contains the socle. This makes all such ideals exactly the preimages of subspaces of m/m², plus zero and R; their products are determined by bilinear orthogonality. Gaussian-binomial counts give the precise C_r orthogonal ordered pairs and all k-factor nonzero-product counts. The degree inequality r²/3 < 2 floor(r²/4) for r>=2 proves the field-size threshold. Direct exhaustive independent ideal enumeration over six small prime-field forms matches pair and triple zero-product counts; finite checks are corroboration only.

value.rationale: The 2026 ideal zero-product invariant has closed published treatments mainly of principal and chain ring families; the new all-length complete distribution covers a natural nonprincipal Gorenstein stratum over arbitrary finite fields and local ring characteristics. The bilinear-form universality, explicit field-size dependence at fixed Loewy length, and sharp 2-to-3 factor threshold are mathematically motivated structural consequences of ideal product dynamics, not merely a normalization or arbitrary finite slice.
